research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-2982, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-1940 refines in place under this same id. Written by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py from the sheet 35x trace (s35xfp-calumet_2008-b1), the T-2982 census (s35x-2008-front) and the T-1837 register row frontage-35x-2008 (Chateauesque brownstone); every height, roof, opening and feature is the draft rules' reconstruction (data/components/prairie_1904/draft_prairie_1904.json; liberty L-draft-district-edges-2982).

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-2982 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

position.note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 20.000, v -0.250 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check: its own fit residual is 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, a similarity on two degrees of freedom that says little away from them, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of trace on this coarser copy. draft_elevation.note: RECONSTRUCTED by the draft rules, family row 'Chateauesque' overlaid with the frontage row: The register's brownstone house under a steep hipped roof with tall chimneys (the Inland Architect plate of December 1883): the steep hip in brownstone. The sheet faces its Calumet front and south side in stone over a brick body; the gabled dormers, the round-arched oriel, the corner projection's roof and the columned porch are T-1940's. Heights are the rules' starting values inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's ranges; bays, entrance side, chimneys and dormers are counts the family rules choose, and the seed 2702544919 only tints the fabric inside +-6 %.
